notes.title: Alpha 2.7.1 - Escort Battles
notes.notes:
Today's build adds the new Escort mission type. You can get this mission from any town. 

Once you have the mission, a ship wheel will appear on your compass directing you to the merchant ship.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/757474342078158167d09e35eba7ca79290cd0c4.png[/img]

You can also find the merchant ship on the overhead map.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/89adcd2dc9d5d6b97143086d1af461e2779622b3.png[/img]

When you arrive, the merchant ship will be locked in battle against pirates. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/ab77bd599eb1322ce04cae6cfeb6d1b9b6ad4f83.png[/img]
I originally had this set up so you would escort the ship (meaning fly with it) in the overhead map and pirates would find it and attack, but this was actually really boring. So I changed it to have the battle ready to go as soon as you arrived.

Once in the battle, your ships will form up as usual, with the addition of the merchant ship behind your ships.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/4e1396297c1acb7d1c95e705be20eba39b6e439c.png[/img]
The merchant ship is treated as one of your ships, except you cannot give it orders. In the screenshot, I have 3 ships and the final hit point bar is the merchant ship. Merchant ships have less hit points than their battle ready counterparts.

If the merchant ship is destroyed, your are reduced to zero hit points, or all of your ships are retreating, then the battle is lost and the mission is failed.

If the merchant ship reaches it's destination (a glowing circle behind the enemy ships) or you destroy all of the enemy ships, then you win the battle and the mission is a success!

This update also includes:
[list][*]Added the gold reward for completing a mission to the animated quest complete UI.
[*]Fixed a bug that caused npc ships to max out at rank 2 rather than rank 3.
[*]Slightly reduced the gold reward for the destroy rival convoy mission.
[*]Slightly increased the gold reward for the protect merchant mission.[/list]
Once I have all of the mission types in the game I will probably add some more aspects to them. For example, you may need a certain level of notoriety with a faction before you can take an escort mission from them. I'll also be using the different mission types as part of the story.

notes.title: Pirate Dragons' Future Plans
notes.notes:
Pirate Dragons has been live for about a month and now that things have settled down a bit, I wanted to take a moment to talk about the future plans I have for the game!

[h2][b]New Battle Types[/b][/h2]
I'm working on a variety of battle types that can be used on their own or as part of a mission or quest. Note, some of these are only in the design phase so the details may change. Also I may decide to not do one or some of these if they aren't fun.
[list][*][b]Destroy Enemy Ships[/b] - this is the current battle scenario.
[*][b]Escort[/b] - a battle that requires you to protect another ship until the ship makes it so specific location in the battle map. At first this will be a new mission type to get in towns, however it can also be used for more story based content such as ensuing a governor makes it back to  their town safely or guarding a ship with a specific, important cargo. Use the tactical map to order your ships to intercept enemy vessels and use breath weapons like ice to block off enemy ships. To win, the escort ship must survive, meaning you don't have to destroy all of the enemy ships to win.
[*][b]Take and Hold[/b] - use the tactical map ([i]did you know there is a tactical map in the battles!? There is! Press M to open it![/i]) to tell your ships to sail to a specific location and stay there until an objective is completed. Sample uses for this could be pillaging an outpost, picking up loot (perhaps the floating loot event uses this too!) or capture the flag style gameplay. Destroy the outpost's defenses so they don't blow apart your ships while they pillage. As above, you don't have to destroy all of the enemy ships. You win when take each point.
[*][b]Destroy Outposts/Forts[/b] - a normal battle except the enemy has small fortifications that must be destroyed. In this battle, you also don't have to destroy the enemy ships to win. Although leaving them alone means a LOT of cannonballs coming your way!
[*][b]Defend Location[/b] - in this mode, you'll either be defending a fort or defending a damaged ship or some other object that can't move. This battle has a countdown timer and you will have to hold off waves of enemy ships until reinforcements arrive. Depending on balance, this mode might have more balloon powerups from your ships or even from whatever you are defending. Having healing breath will be very important in this mode to keep your ships afloat![/list]I have the escort battle working right now. The others are in various states of design or early development.

[h2][b]Factions and Economy[/b][/h2]
I want to make factions more meaningful.
[list][*][b]Notoriety [/b]- gaining positive notoriety will unlock mission types and quests. Gaining negative notoriety already causes factions to send convoys to attack you. I'd like to add a bit more to this as well. Also, I want faction notoriety to improve slowly over time if you have negative notoriety. This allows you to get out of the bottom if you leave a faction alone for a while. High notoriety will not decrease over time.
[*][b]Economy Balance [/b]- right now there isn't really a need to buy and trade goods because battles yield a lot of resources. I want trading to matter more while also keeping battles rewards. Right now you can go over your maximum cargo from battles. I left this in because I didn't have a clear way for you to know you are at cargo capacity and fighting a battle and getting nothing from it would be a negative experience. Once I do some more work on the economy, and surface your cargo capacity better, I'll likely start to enforce the max capacity. Also, right now each resource has one price for buying and selling. I did that to keep things simple, but I might change this so resources have a buy price and a sell price. This would allow me to have factions give you a discount on the sale price without also automatically lowing the buy price. For each town, the price to sell resources will never be higher than the price to buy them though of course. This will require a pretty big update to the Trading UI as well as having a big impact on the economy, so I will probably not do this part any time soon.
[*][b]Faction Resource Focus[/b] - right now the factions already focus on different resources but I don't communicate that well. I'd like to make this more obvious and also have factions request resources they are running out of, essentially creating a mission opportunity that is based on the actual state of the economy.
[*]Economy State Changes - like the above, your actions already affect the economy. So if you destroy a convoy that is carrying fish and it's on it's way to the town of Trensec, the cost of fish will go up in Trensec because those fish never arrived. Again, this isn't communicated well so I want to improve that and make this even more meaningful.
[*][b]Faction Differences [/b]- I want to add some differences between the factions. For example, Verrxenn might make better cannons, Baphel better captains, Alporee better crew, and Pithariee focuses on hulls. To get rank 3 in one of those ship parts, you'll need to go to a faction town that specializes in that part. Your notoriety will affect the cost of that upgrade and if your notoriety is super low, the faction may refuse to upgrade your ship unless you do something to gain their favor first.
[/list]
[h2][b]Story[/b][/h2]
I have the beginnings of an overarching story that I want to add to the game. Taking part in the quests associated with the story will be optional but may unlock some aspects of game play. I'm still working through this so it may be a bit further in the future.

[h2][b]Miscellaneous Stuff[/b][/h2]
Some other things I want to work on:
[list][*][b]Full Controller Support[/b] - you can use a controller to play, but full support means adding a virtual keyboard, adding controller support for slider bars in the settings UI, changing the controls text when using a controller, and controller button mapping.
[*][b]Steam Deck[/b] - Pirate Dragons already works on Steam Deck (including the built-in virtual keyboard) but I can't officially request certification. Hopefully Valve will look at Pirate Dragons and give the thumbs up some time soon. If there is any work to get verified, I'll make it a high priority,
[*][b]Quality of Life[/b] - mostly doing a better job surfacing things like quest rewards when you complete a quest, faction notoriety, more settings options, and other things that will make Pirate Dragons more enjoyable to play![/list]
This is a pretty big list for one developer, so it may take me a while to get to all of it! I would love to hear your thoughts on these ideas as well as hearing your own ideas!

Thank you for all of the feedback and support everyone! A

nd, don't forget to join the Pirate Dragons discord!

-Jonathan "Calandryll" Hanna

notes.title: Alpha 1.0.6 - Retreating and Losing Battles
notes.notes:
Today's build adds losing battles to the game. Prior to this update you would never lose a battle as I was still deciding how that would work.

With this update, you lose a battle if...
[list][*]Your health is reduced to zero or,
[*]All of your ships hull points are reduced to zero.[/list]
When your health is reduced to zero, the battle ends. You do not receive any XP for yourself or your ships and do not get any loot. There is no death penalty beyond that for now and you can immediately continue exploring in the overworld map.

When one of your ships has its hull points reduced to zero, that ship will retreat. A retreating ship does not fire its cannons nor does it take fire from enemies. Your nature breath will also not heal the ship. It is considered out of the battle and will sail back towards your starting location. A retreating ship loses all of it's upgrades to the captain, crew, cannons, and hull - but the ship is not lost and you don't have to rebuy it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/98fd02c29f09e32084afe550385e2cfd1f6df95d.png[/img]

If all of your ships retreat, the battle immediately ends.

If you win a battle, but had one or more ships that were retreating those ships also lose their progression, but your dragon and any ships that were not retreating do gain XP and you do gain the loot from the convoy you were victorious against.

After a battle, win or lose, your ships and your dragon are returned to full health.

This update also includes a few other updates:
[list][*]Loading a save now correctly loads all of the convoy data including the cargo for all of the convoys.
[*]You can close the ship information UI when examining a ship in the overhead map by clicking outside of that UI.
[*]Clicking track ship on compass will also close that window.[/list]

With losing battles now in the game, most of the main features are complete. I'll be refining these based on feedback and will be adding more content in the next few updates. I'll also be adding more settings, options, and quality of life updates.

Thank you again to everyone participating in the playtest!

notes.title: Playtest Build, Alpha 1.0!
notes.notes:
Today's playtest update is a big one! It includes all of the main islands for the game world, an overhead map, enemy wyvrens, the first pass at the dynamic economy, events, rumors, a save/load system, and a lot more!

[h1][b]World and Factions[/b][/h1]
All of the major islands are built for the game world. There are 35 islands with about 28 towns across four factions. I will be adding smaller islands to add a bit more interest between the larger islands. The world is also separated between the four factions and the towns on the islands have different styles based on the faction. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/37c7a8f0567dad07e086130a6ebc9d3a7fb7b6ef.png[/img]

Each faction now has primary resources that they produce. Convoys from a faction are more likely to be carrying these resources and prices will vary depending on whether a faction produces a resource or not. More no this later.

Ship convoys are separated between "ocean going" and regular. Regular convoys tend to stay near their faction islands while ocean going can travel across the entire map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/2d38efbe363ec0b25990c8ab5ef8bb87ba80493b.png[/img]

Faction colors and symbols are now created after you create your faction. This ensures that the NPC factions never use the same colors or symbol that you used.

[h1][b]Combat[/b][/h1]
Some ships can be designated as wyvren carries. These ships will spawn wyvrens during a battle. Wyvrens prioritize attacking your ships their fire breath is just as deadly as yours! They are vulnerable to your fire breath however and can also be downed by the swivel guns on your ships.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/4c719c734b1c54ebbc4149557671412dda95f738.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/6391bbaf1b274ee1a9fe7bf50aaac628fc92f0e2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/ee5640afea2442a08551344938a31dd8709e7238.png[/img]

Damage to ships is now shown by how many of its sails are on fire. The more damaged a ship is, the more of its sails will burn. The Guppy class of ship has three sails now (originally it only had one) so you can tell how damaged it is within this system. I also created a tutorial UI to explain how to attack ships and how the sail fire damage indicator works.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/2f0cceb59819aadc1eec0246a604f8bb5021d459.png[/img]

Swivel guns now shoot in volleys rather than independently. This allows you to get in close and breath fire on ships in-between their swivel gun shots. Swivel gun cannonballs also trail fire to differentiate them from the main cannon shots, which trail smoke.

All ships now react when hit by the lightning attack. The lightning attack pushes down on the ship, causing it to lower into the ocean a bit and reducing it's speed. This allows you to use the lightning attack not only to cause damage, but to also influence the movement of the enemy ships.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/b10365aa6af18d7c2f7e189bc8fc7fba05cb71a8.png[/img]

When you are looking at a ship during combat, the health UI for that ship will be highlighted. This makes it easier to tell which ship you are attacking, especially during larger fights!

Added sound effects your dragon's cannons reload and when attempting to use a breath weapon that is out of charges.

If one of your ships is destroyed, you now lose cargo based on what percentage of your maximum cargo that ship represented. 

Note right now you can't lose a battle. If you lose all of your ships you will get two free ships to continue playing. I'm still deciding what losing a battle will mean, whether you can retreat, and what happens if you are killed and/or all of your ships are destroyed.

[h1][b]Economy[/b][/h1]
Faction convoys are separated in two categories, ocean going and local. Local convoys will stay closer to their faction area, usually only delivering cargo between different faction controlled islands. Ocean going convoys can travel to any island on the map and will be the primary driver of the eventual dynamic economy system. As cargo is delivered across factions, prices will vary depending on what cargo a faction needs and what resources were delivered. 

Destroying a convoy will affect the prices of the resources that convoy was carrying at the town they were headed towards. Doing this will also negatively impact your faction standing with BOTH the ships' faction and the destination town's faction.

You can have up to four ships in your convoy. There is a button in the Docks UI to allow you to dismiss a ship if you are at the maximum and want to purchase a new ship.

[h1][b]User Interface[/b][/h1]  
The battle victory UI has been updated to more clearly reflect the XP, gold, and cargo you gained from the battle. 

The world map UI has been updated to show all 35 islands and the locations of convoys. The ship icon's sails are colored to match the faction color and the icons move in real time while the map is open. You can also click on a convoy to see its cargo and where it is headed.

The event UI has been updated to give more information regarding the result of your choice. I also added an event result screen that displays confirming the result and giving information regarding any other information. 

Added a delete save button to the title screen UI so you can start over and test earlier parts of the game if you want to.

The settings UI now includes options for sound and music volume

[h1][b]Events and Rumors[/b][/h1] 
Added locations for two new events, floating loot and buried treasure. Floating loot can appear anywhere in the ocean while buried treasure tends to appear on the uninhabited islands or on larger town islands, but away from the town.

You can speak with a tavernkeeper once per day to learn about a good price for a resource at another town. I'll be adding more types of rumors, such as a ship carrying specific cargo and quest related information as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/4799935cbac4fc6376779f0261da2a27127e21bc.png[/img]

[h1][b]Save System[/b][/h1] 
Your progress is now saved between sessions. The game automatically saves every time you open the ESC UI and when finishing a battle. I'll be adding more to this as I add more features.

All of these updates bring Pirate Dragons to Alpha 1.0 and the game is getting very close to feature complete! 

If you haven't already, be sure to sign up for the playtest and wishlist Pirate Dragons!

notes.title: Playtest Update
notes.notes:
I wanted to write a quick update on the Pirate Dragons playtest. First, thank you to everyone who has given my feedback.

I'm working on a few systems that I want to have in the game before starting the next playtest round. 
[list][*] Factions and Faction Reputation
[*] Quests/Missions
[*] Events[/list]
I'm hoping to have them all in and working next week. 

A quick synopsis of each feature.

There are 4 main [b]factions [/b]and 3 pirate factions in the world. You will have different reputation with each. A positive reputation will mean lower prices on repairs and upgrades and a low reputation will mean higher prices. A very low reputation may even result in that faction sending ships to attack you and/or refusing to give you quests or missions. Increasing your reputation with a faction will also unlock more quests and missions with that faction.

[b]Quests and Missions[/b] are usually given by the factions. Quests are one-offs and story driven, such as being asked to attack a specific pirate who has swindled a faction. Missions work pretty much the same as quests, but are repeatable and may include something like delivering goods from one town to another. Completing quests and missions will be one of the ways you can increase your reputation with a faction.

[b]Events [/b]can be found in the game, usually in the overworld view. These are multiple choice situations that can lead to treasure, faction notoriety changes, other rewards, and even ambushes. Below is an example of an event.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/537c2c3f232e26e89a91e9379dc44b285f028229.png[/img]
[i](art is placeholder)[/i]

Basically once these features are in, you'll be able to play a small sample of the game loop. The game will still feel grindy and it isn't balanced yet though. But anyone who wants to give feedback on the game will be able to play this build and have enough of an experience to get a sense of what the game will be. If I have time, I also want to hook up the save/load game system so you can progress without having to play for a long time all at once.

I'll be writing more information about these systems in the coming days. If you haven't signed up for the playtest yet now is a good time to do so! I will be inviting [b]everyone[/b] who signs up once the build is ready, hopefully in a week or two!

I'm very excited to be able to share Pirate Dragons with all of you and I'm looking forward to hear what you think of the game!

notes.title: Factions
notes.notes:
Factions play an important role in Pirate Dragons as they control the towns where you can trade goods, upgrade ships, and learn new skills. There are four factions created randomly at the start of a new game. Each faction will have distinct colors and a faction symbol that is displayed on their flags and their ships' main sail.

The factions are created after you've chosen your faction colors, style, and symbol. The AI factions then use the remining choices, so they'll never use the same options as you've chosen. Factions can have different personalities - some may focus on trading goods, others may be quick to go to war, and others may take it upon themselves to rid the world of pirates. How aggressive the factions will likely be something you can set before starting a new game.

Attack and destroy a faction's ships or pirate their cargo, and you'll make an enemy pretty quickly! At the same time, you may make a new friend if two factions are rivals.

notes.title: Ships and Crews
notes.notes:
If you want to be successful in Pirate Dragons, you're going to need to enlist some ships and people to crew them! Ships are the main way to transport large amounts of goods (although Dragons are highly sought after to deliver small items such as important documents and jewelry on their own) and allies if you find yourself in a battle.

Ships in Pirate Dragons are made up of the Captain, the Crew, Cannons, Sails, and the Hull. Each part of a ship can be upgraded, either through gaining experience or through buying better versions. Experience can be earned in combat as well as through other methods such as trading goods or completing quests. A small ship with a highly rated captain and crew and upgraded cannons, can take on much larger ships that lack highly rated components.

[h3]Ship Captain[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/7a90884bdbfb0a44208024c6108987d9abbd657d.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/7a90884bdbfb0a44208024c6108987d9abbd657d.png[/img][/url]
[i][ click image to see full size and pirate speak ][/i]

The captain is responsible for steering the ship, affects the overall skill of the crew, and often has a special skill. Captains are rated between 1 and 5 stars. The higher the rating, the more effective the captain.

You can hire captains at the various towns in the world. Captains can level up and improve the more experience they get. They can also be injured or killed in battle.

The captain affects how maneuverable the ship is and how quickly a ship reacts to changes in a battle. Captains who have a special skill can perform actions during a battle, such as a speed boost for a short duration or a hard turn. 

[h3]Ship Crew[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/679e9a8f561af112d66d9d370cd1f4f93c7e40fb.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/679e9a8f561af112d66d9d370cd1f4f93c7e40fb.png[/img][/url]
[i][ click image to see full size and pirate speak ][/i]

A ship is nothing without its crew - and its sails, cannons, hull, and lots of other parts – but it’s the crew that bring a ship to life!

Crews are rated from 1 star to 5 stars. A crew’s rating cannot be higher than the captain’s rating. So, for a ship to have 3 star crew, it must have a captain of 3 stars or higher.

The crew is responsible for reloading and shooting the cannons, repairing the ship during a battle, and putting out fires. The more stars a crew has the better they are at each of their responsibilities. A very high star crew makes for a very dangerous and difficult to fight ship!

[h3]Cannons[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/c31e787dda478a75e28dde4d569c7a711ff3c500.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/c31e787dda478a75e28dde4d569c7a711ff3c500.png[/img][/url]
[i][ click image to see full size and pirate speak ][/i]

There are two kinds of cannons, the swivel guns and the main cannons. Swivel guns are used to shoot at targets in the air such as dragons or wyvrens. The main guns are mostly used against other ships, however a low flying creature can be hit by a cannonball fired by a main gun.

Cannons have different quality levels which affect how accurate their shots are, the damage of their cannonballs, in addition to the chance of a cannonball setting a fire on impact.

[h3]Sails and Hulls[/h3]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/6b5a5e2e5464e1d6cd7cd584704fd2a35e5c5a8e.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/6b5a5e2e5464e1d6cd7cd584704fd2a35e5c5a8e.png[/img][/url]
[i][ click image to see full size and pirate speak ][/i]

The sails of a ship affect how fast it can go. Better sails offer better speed in addition to being more fire resistant.

A ship’s hull affects how sturdy the ship is. In game terms, this is basically the ship’s hit points. A hull also affects a ship’s speed and maneuverability. The best way to cause damage to a ship is to set fires on it either from cannonballs or fire breath.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/909ca0088dd13c089f3eb983360024da094f1b4f.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/909ca0088dd13c089f3eb983360024da094f1b4f.png[/img][/url]

With twice the cannons and 50% more health, in this battle, the larger ship easily defeats the smaller ship. But, when the small ship is outfitted with a 5 star captain, a 5 star crew, and upgraded cannons, the little ship can win the day - albeit, barely!

Don't forget to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1835120/Pirate_Dragons/][u][b]Wishlist Pirate Dragons[/b][/u][/url] if you haven't already!

notes.title: Breath Weapons
notes.notes:
There are five breath weapons available to your dragon. Fire, Acid, Ice, Water, and Nature. Each breath weapon has its unique use in a battle. As you adventure, you'll be able to learn and improve breath weapons, making them even more effective.

[h3]Fire[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/a0e9cfcbf89ac81e686be7eb15833ed125b866c2.gif[/img]
The fire breath weapon is the primary way you inflict damage on ships, wyverns, dragons, and other enemies. Setting fires on a ship's hull is the best way do damage to it while setting a ship's sails ablaze reduces its maneuverability and distracts the crew from reloading and shooting their cannons. The more powerful your fire breath the more fires you can set.

[h3]Acid[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/67d9ef3496789c6d25f5aa9bbc3582b5f47c58cf.gif[/img]
The acid breath weapon is a great way to "debuff" a ship. The acid damages the ship's cannons and creates a green mist that slows down the ship's crew. This is particularly useful when fighting a large ship with many upgraded cannons and a well trained crew. The more powerful your acid breath the longer it lasts.

[h3]Ice[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/780d40acc77b8055c7f8d88e0a18a9185eab9d6a.gif[/img]
Breathing the ice breath weapon into the ocean will create columns of ice that can block a ship's progress and block their cannon balls. A very useful attack if you want to steer an enemy ship in a certain direction or keep it from attacking and damaging one of your ships. Increasing the power of your ice breath allows you to create more ice columns and makes them to last longer.

[h3]Water[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/861a6c7b9209b440468ca5472aac29f21cbb0cd3.gif[/img]
The water breath weapon is primary used to put out fires on a ship. The water breath also soaks the ship, making it immune to fires for a short period of time. The more powerful your water breath, the longer the soaking lasts.

[h3]Nature[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42266967/cfca7230d7116149b6e82e2a70506887ad0dc71c.gif[/img]
Breathing your nature breath on a ship will create vines and leaves that reinforce and patch up a damaged wooden ship. Essentially this allows you to heal your ships. Having a more powerful nature breath means healing more damage.

It is possible for a dragon to learn all five breath weapons, although only the most powerful are able to master all five. Most only learn 2 or 3. Wyverns are only capable of using one - usually fire.

Stay tuned for more updates, including how ship upgrades work, the overland map, leveling up, the economy, and more!
